sampling_model.design: Fixed finite family of perfect-intervention settings \(v=(S,x)\), where \(x=0\) or a unit coordinate vector in \(\mathbb R^S\).
sampling_model.units: For the statistical rung, \(m\) independent equilibrium observations are drawn in every retained setting; population identification uses the full response kernels.
sampling_model.treatment: A treatment sets every observed coordinate in \(S\) to \(x\) and preserves the remaining equations and source laws.
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment-overlap condition is needed because regimes are designed; every retained regime has \(m\) draws.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No source separation is performed. Empirical characteristic functions at \(J_m\) computable rational frequencies are compared with globally certified compact-model characteristic functions.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Dai et al. characterize observational distributional equivalence for the zero-allowed linear non-Gaussian latent cyclic class.
Latent directed acyclic graphs are hard-intervention equivalent exactly when their intervention-indexed augmented maximal ancestral graphs satisfy the stated skeleton and collider criteria.
The pair condition together with the covariance condition is necessary and sufficient for full recovery of a linear cyclic model from experimental means and covariances.

Proposition 5.1 states that the observational distribution together with the atomic interventional distribution for coordinate \(i\) recovers row \(i\) of the square coefficient matrix, hence its parents and causal effects.
Aligned single-target equilibrium response maps identify a latent cyclic mechanism under full target coverage, with a graph-dependent characterization when one target is missing.
Cross-cumulant tensor rank restrictions yield goodness-of-fit tests for latent linear non-Gaussian structural equation models.
Inverting graph-indexed goodness-of-fit tests yields asymptotically valid confidence sets for causal orderings in acyclic additive-error models.

body.tldr: The paper gives sound-and-complete finite criteria, with certified compilers, for equality of joint perfect-intervention response-kernel law sets in latent cyclic linear non-Gaussian models under both exact-support and zero-allowed graph conventions, for fixed observed and latent node sets. At the observational specialization, the zero-allowed theorem matches Dai et al.’s published model class; for a general finite intervention family it adds simultaneous principal-response constraints ensuring that one coefficient matrix and one source-law tuple realize every regime. The exact-support stratum engine combines affine and Hall–Rado realization, unrestricted visible-source partitions, and translation rigidity while retaining cancellations, invisible sources, and lower-dimensional strata. The paper also proves the moment-free square no-latent row and matching reduction, an all-parameter exact-support strict-refinement witness, and an honest compact-Laplace graph confidence superset.

project_justification.gap: Dai et al. characterize observational distributional equivalence for zero-allowed latent cyclic linear non-Gaussian models, Zhou et al. characterize graphical hard-intervention equivalence for latent directed acyclic graphs, and Hyttinen, Eberhardt, and Hoyer address full second-order recovery under richer experiments. None characterizes equality of joint perfect-intervention response-kernel law sets for latent cyclic linear non-Gaussian models under the requirement that one coefficient matrix and one source-law tuple realize all regimes, including cancellations and invisible or merged sources.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a finite coupled invariant that simultaneously represents punctured structural completion, invisible or merged independent sources, principal intervention responses, and common-mechanism gluing on every lower-dimensional stratum.
project_justification.fill: The proposed criterion reduces admissible mechanisms to graph-generated affine and rank charts, reduces arbitrary source-law containment to finite proportional-column surjections, couples regimes through principal response matrices, and asks for an explicit certified compiler with a size-dependent bit bound. The inferential rung compares observable characteristic functions directly on a compact subclass.

body.related_work: Dai et al., Theorem 2, characterize observational distributional equivalence for irreducible zero-allowed latent cyclic linear non-Gaussian models after their reduction step. At \(\mathcal I=\{\varnothing\}\) and fixed latent cardinality, \(\texttt{thm:zero-allowed-coupled-equivalence}\) uses the same structural and source class; for general \(\mathcal I\), it extends the law-set target to joint perfect-intervention kernels generated by one common mechanism. Zhou et al. encode hard-intervention invariances for latent directed acyclic graphs through augmented maximal ancestral graphs; their object is graphical constraint equivalence rather than equality of cyclic parametric response-kernel sets. Bongers et al. supply the solvability semantics that justify imposing invertibility separately after every intervention; the stronger uniform singular-value margin used only in the inference subclass is not their assumption or result. Hyttinen, Eberhardt, and Hoyer give necessary and sufficient experiment-design conditions for full second-order recovery, which is a different target from the quotient under an arbitrary fixed intervention family. Sharifian et al., Proposition 5.1, establish published row recovery for coordinate \(i\) in a square no-latent model from observational and randomized atomic-intervention distributions. Separately, the internal node \(\texttt{thm:no-latent-reduction-moment-free}\) proves the square projection, translation lift, moment-free response-kernel row-recovery map, and matching-set equality; only its row-recovery clause matches Sharifian et al., Proposition 5.1. Taeb et al. and Joint Causal Inference make shared mechanisms across environments explicit, but do not provide the required cyclic non-Gaussian common-lift theorem. Dadgostari and Nazemi study aligned response matrices for sensing an entirely latent equilibrium state and identify a single mechanism under target coverage or support conditions; they do not compare graph-indexed full-law sets under observed-node perfect interventions, arbitrary independent sources, and exact cancellations. Schkoda and Drton provide rank-based goodness-of-fit tests, while Wang, Kolar, and Drton provide test inversion for acyclic orderings; the statistical rung instead tests full observable law-set proximity for compact latent feedback models.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The \(N=4\) forced-zero, latent-rank, degenerate-pivot, and rational-witness checks are diagnostics rather than substitutes for the proved universal realization and source-partition arguments. The displayed compiler bound is deliberately conservative and is not claimed optimal. The strict-refinement witness proves refinement over observational equivalence but does not establish failure of the implication from equality of every separate regime projection to joint equality; realizability and the smallest such graph pair remain the stated open problem.
body.honest_scope: The population results are uniform over each fixed finite observed set, latent cardinality, and intervention family, and require only mutually independent nonconstant non-Gaussian sources, without centering or moments. At the observational specialization, the zero-allowed class agrees with Dai et al.’s published model class at fixed latent cardinality; their graphical theorem is formulated after irreducible reduction, whereas the present subgraph-stratified criterion explicitly retains reducible, invisible-source, and lower-dimensional strata. The results do not compare different latent cardinalities in one run. The strict-refinement witness is an exact-support result and no analogous zero-allowed separation is claimed. Under no latent variables, the observational projection is the square perfect-matching object and atomic kernels restrict it by recovered row labels; Sharifian et al., Proposition 5.1, supplies only the published row-recovery comparator. Covariance is used only on the finite-second-moment witness submodel, and statistical certification is restricted to the compact Laplace subclass. The rooted-gluing proposition is complete as a finite criterion, while realizability and minimality of a graph-generated failure of separate-to-joint implication remain open.
